findings.title: Negative offsets allowed in OptimizedCursorPaginator, and Django rejects negative slicing
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:0` gives a 500. Even if it worked, the comment claiming this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level is wrong. Negative offsets are a way around the pagination bounds. The cursor comes from user input, and nothing validates it. Reject negative offsets instead of enabling them.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offset to queryset slicing for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` leaves negative offsets unclamped for any prev cursor. This affects every endpoint that uses BasePaginator, not only the new paginator. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-1:1`) now reaches `queryset[-1:stop]`, which raises an AssertionError (500). Before this change the slice was `queryset[offset:stop]`, which also had no clamp, so the change adds nothing and its comment claiming safety is false. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down also mixes up the offsets.

findings.title: Unreleased experimental pagination path gated on client-controlled flag in an audit-log endpoint
findings.body: The audit log endpoint is unrelated to the spans buffer change in the PR title. It adds an `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter that switches to a paginator accepting negative offsets. This is exposed to superusers and to any member with global access. Giving privileged users a less-validated cursor path on a sensitive audit log is risky, and the paginator has no tests. This should be a separate, reviewed change. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` also duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result` almost entirely. Its `get_item_key` is the plain integer one, which would fail on the datetime `-datetime` ordering used here: `math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError on organization_context.member
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the organization. `request.user.is_superuser or ...` short-circuits for superusers. For non-superusers without a membership, `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. The expression is also evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested, so it can break the default path.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace
findings.body: Lines 71 and 89 have trailing whitespace (also in paginator.py docstring lines). This will fail the repo's lint checks.

findings.title: Redirect loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification
findings.body: The loop bound went from 10000 to 1000, and the comment that documented the limit was dropped. Segment trees deeper than 1000 hops will now be joined incorrectly. Nothing in the PR says this is intentional, and it is unrelated to the eviction feature.

findings.title: Eviction trims by score order using hardcoded 1000 and is inconsistent with max_segment_spans
findings.body: Eviction uses a hardcoded 1000 limit, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` is 1001 (and no longer enforced in `_load_segment_data`). `span_count` is only the zunionstore result from the last merge, or a zcard. Because `zpopmin` removes the lowest-score (earliest end timestamp) spans, a segment's root or early spans can be dropped silently, with no metric or log. The old explicit check and the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric were removed, so there is no visibility. The `max_segment_spans` parameter is now dead.

findings.title: Switching set to sorted set breaks compatibility with existing keys and drops required field handling
findings.body: Switching from SADD/SSCAN to ZADD/ZSCAN changes the Redis type of `span-buf:s:*` keys. Existing set keys in a live deployment will cause WRONGTYPE errors on `zadd`, `zcard` and `zunionstore`, with no migration or rollout note. Also, `end_timestamp_precise` is read with `val[...]`, which raises KeyError for any span lacking the field, crashing the whole batch. Identical payloads are deduplicated by member, as with sets, so the score of a re-sent span is updated.

findings.title: __reduce__ does not pass the new/reordered constructor args correctly
findings.body: `__reduce__` passes `redis_ttl` positionally as the 4th argument, but the 4th parameter of `__init__` is `segment_page_size`. This is a pre-existing bug, but it matters now because the segment limits are central to this change. Pickled instances in multiprocessing get the wrong `segment_page_size`.
